column1: # golden_bands.tsv -- the ONE table that says how wide a golden row's band is,
# by WHAT KIND OF NUMBER the row holds (C384, 2026-11-13).  Read by
# bin/curate/golden_bands.py, which is the recorder's band writer
# (bin/runTests --record), the tool that rewrote the existing goldens, and the
# library of bin/curate/check_golden_bands.py (the gate that holds every row to
# its class).  A row of NO class below is a DIRECT RESULT: the default 1e-4 (a
# case may author another band for it; the gate does not police that).
# Columns (TAB separated):  class | kinds | name regex | key regex | rule | param | reason
#   kinds       comma list of golden kinds the class applies to
#   name regex  matched (fullmatch) against the row's name column; `.*` = any
#   key regex   matched (fullmatch) against the row's key column
#   rule        rel  -- a relative band, `param` is the number
#               abs_frac_of_term -- an ABSOLUTE band `abs:<param x term>`;
#                   which term is named by the `term` rule in golden_bands.py
#                   (boundary_denominator | unit_Q_kW | ledger_terms)
#   Floor: an absolute band is never written below 1e-9 in the row's own unit.
# The first matching line wins.  Anchor rows and `exact` rows are never touched.
count
column7: A count of iterations or evaluations is decided by comparisons of 1e-6 on a max-norm objective (FitObjective.cpp minimise: restart ends when the best value improved by less than 1e-6 relative), so it is chaotic in the last digits: measured 2265 of 4174 minimax_evaluations rows differ between two platforms, max 1.43 from 5 restart passes against 2.  The row asserts "within a factor of three" and still fails a solver that needs ten times more.

column1: condition
column7: The condition number of J^T J in a flat valley moves with the last digits of the parameters: measured median 2.3e-3, p95 0.22, max 1.4e3 between two platforms.  Rows still red are pinned findings (platform_divergence_debt.tsv).

column1: parameter
column7: A fitted parameter is defined to about sqrt of the least-squares tolerance (FitParameters.cpp:662, tolerance 1e-4 on the relative change of chi2) in the flat directions of J^T J; measured p95 0.19 and max 0.35.  Five times that square root; rows still red are findings.

column1: objective
column7: A statistic of an optimiser's answer inherits its stopping tolerance (least squares 1e-4 on the change of chi2): a hundred times that.  Measured median 1.2e-3, p95 0.09, max 0.39; rows still red are flat-valley findings, not a wider class.

column1: residual_boundary
column7: A closure residual is round-off of a balance, so it is compared on an ABSOLUTE band written in the row: 1e-5 of the energy the plant exchanges (`residual_denom_kW` of the same result block; measured platform difference at most 6.4e-7 of it).  With no published denominator: abs:max(1e-3 kW, 1e-4 x |expected|) -- the 1e-3 kW floor, never tighter than the relative 1e-4 the row always had (flash20 differs by 4.3e-3 kW of 42.86 between two runs on one platform).

column1: residual_hx
column7: The gap is the unit's own enthalpy closure in the unit of its duty: 1e-8 of that unit's |Q_kW| (measured 1e-10).

column1: residual_ledger
column7: The campaign and dynamic energy ledgers: 1e-9 of the largest pinned energy term of that ledger (measured 6e-13 and 2e-15).
